title: Controlled Chaos Experimentation Library and Runbook
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary:
This document is a centralized library and operational runbook for controlled chaos experiments (CCE) on the Redwood Inference platform. It defines a catalog of reproducible simulations, safety controls, preflight checks, dashboards and alert templates, the execution runbook, and a short roadmap for institutionalizing CCE as part of our platform hardening practice.

Why we run controlled chaos:
- Validate fallback and circuit-breaker behavior under realistic degraded conditions.
- Surface gaps in routing, KV cache, and batcher assumptions before customer impact.
- Exercise SRE and platform runbooks in a low-risk, observable way.

Goals and success criteria:
- All experiments have non-customer-facing blast radius and an automated abort.
- Observable metrics show expected degradation pattern and then recovery within SLOs; if not, roll forward fixes and a postmortem within 2 weeks.
- Each experiment produces a dashboard, a test harness entry, and at least one runbook refinement.

Scope and non-goals:
- Scope: infra and control-plane interactions, request routing, caching, autoscaling, model-variant fallback, rate-limit behaviors, and burst isolation.
- Non-goals: model quality regressions, long-running data migration testing, or experiments that require cross-account customer data.

Safety and governance (mandatory):
1) Authorization: experiments must be approved by the owning service lead and the on-call SRE.
2) Blast radius fences: experiments run in a dedicated test tenant namespace or isolated staging cluster and are gated by tagging (experiment=true).
3) Kill switch: every experiment must register a heartbeat to the CCE controller and support an immediate abort endpoint (POST /ce/abort).
4) Traffic safety: synthetic injection only; no live customer traffic unless explicitly approved by Product and Security.
5) Escalation: if error-rate > 0.5% on any production route or p95 latency crosses 3x baseline, abort and follow Incident Runbook v2.

Preflight checklist (run before any experiment):
- Ownership and approvers listed in experiment metadata.
- Target cluster, tenant, and node list confirmed and reserved.
- Monitoring: dashboards deployed and alert thresholds configured (see dashboard templates).
- Backup: KV prefixes snapshotted and autoscaler overrides prepared.
- Communication: Slack #platform-experiments and email to oncall+engineering distribution with start window.
- Runbook printed and visible to participants.

Experiment catalog (examples):
1) model-variant-fallback-sim (medium risk)
   - Description: Simulate slow responses from primary model variant to validate automated fallback to quantized variant and metrics carried to tracing.
   - Target: dedicated test pool, prefix-cache warm=on.
   - Expected signal: p50 latency up by 1.5x, p95 spikes, fallback rate > 90% within 60s.
   - Safety: abort on error-rate > 0.2% or fallback rate < 50% after 3 minutes.

2) kv-prefix-eviction-storm (low risk)
   - Description: Force rapid cache evictions to observe prefix-cache miss amplification and hotspot detection.
   - Target: single availability zone test cluster.
   - Expected signal: miss-rate increases, per-host CPU up to 60%, batching latency modestly increased.
   - Safety: auto-throttle eviction script and abort if backend queue length > 1k.

3) control-plane-latency-dilation (high risk, restricted)
   - Description: Inject synthetic latency into control-plane metadata calls to simulate high control-plane latency.
   - Target: gated and requires Security approval.
   - Expected signal: delayed routing decisions, increased circuit-breaker trip.
   - Safety: must run during maintenance window with SRE lead present.

Simulation catalog table (config summary):
| experiment_key | risk | target | abort_condition | owners |
| model-variant-fallback | medium | test-gpu-pool | error_rate>0.2% | inference-runtime team |
| kv-eviction-storm | low | staging-az2 | backend_queue>1000 | cache-team |
| control-latency | high | gated-prod-sim | p95_control_plane>1s | infra-reliability |

Dashboard and alert templates (copy/paste examples):
- Key panels: p50/p95/p99 latency by route, error-rate by route, fallback-rate, cache-hit/miss by prefix, inflight-requests, queue-length, GPU-utilization.
- Prometheus alert example:
  ALERT CCE_FallbackRateLow
  IF sum(rate(fallback_count[1m])) / sum(rate(request_count[1m])) < 0.5
  FOR 3m
  LABELS {severity="page"}
  ANNOTATIONS {summary="Fallback rate below expected during experiment", runbook="/runbooks/cce-fallback"}

Runbook: execution steps (operator checklist)
1) Pre-checks (10–30m): validate preflight items, confirm dashboards, perform dry-run of abort endpoint.
2) Start (T0): enable experiment flag in test namespace. Post start message to #platform-experiments.
3) Monitor (T0+0–15m): watch metrics, ensure expected pattern; if discrepancy, pause and inspect.
4) Scale (if part of experiment): apply autoscaler policy changes incrementally with 5-minute waits.
5) Completion: gracefully ramp down experiment over 10m, revert any config overrides.
6) Post-checks: validate cache integrity, confirm no lingering throttles, and close communication.
7) Postmortem: within 72 hours produce a short retro with findings, actions, and dashboard links.

Incident flow (if experiment causes unexpected production impact):
- Immediate: abort experiment via CCE controller and capture trace links.
- Triage: platform oncall to run Incident Runbook v2 and page appropriate owners.
- Containment: remove experiment tags, scale down affected pools, and apply pre-approved mitigation (traffic-redistribution policy).
- Root-cause: reuse the simulation harness to reproduce at smaller scale and create a mitigation patch.

Templates and artifacts (repository locations):
- Simulation harness repo: github.com/redwood/platform-cce (template playbooks and CICD job).
- Dashboard templates: grafana://dashboards/platform-cce-library (copy for each experiment).
- Abort controller API: POST https://cce-controller.internal/api/v1/abort

Metrics to record for every experiment (minimum):
- request_count, error_count, p50/p95/p99 latency, fallback_rate, cache_hit_rate, gpu_utilization, queue_length, autoscaler_decisions_count

Retrospective highlights (typical findings and actions):
- Common gaps: insufficient tracing metadata to link fallbacks to caller tenant; action: add request-scoped trace tags.
- Operational friction: manual approval delays; action: define stricter guardrails and a template approval flow to speed safe experiments.
- Observability: missing baseline dashboards for certain internal routes; action: onboard route metadata into metrics-collector.

Roadmap (next 12 months):
- Q3 2025: Automate preflight checks and one-click experiment creation in Console.
- Q4 2025: Integrate CCE controller with canary rollout framework to allow cross-checks with live traffic in limited, auditable fashion.
- Q1 2026: Add tenant-aware blast radius controls and cost-estimation of each experiment.

Owner and maintenance cadence:
- Primary owner: Platform Resilience team (owner alias: @platform-resilience).
- Review cadence: quarterly review and exercise of 2 catalog experiments per quarter.

Appendix: quick PromQL snippets (copy/paste)
- p95 latency by route:
  histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, route))
- fallback-rate:
  sum(rate(fallback_count[5m])) by (route) / sum(rate(request_count[5m])) by (route)

Contact and escalation list:
- Platform Resilience: resilience@redwood.com
- Oncall SRE: oncall@redwood-infra.com

Change log:
- 2025-03-11: initial draft (Aisha Patel)
